why: Binary search over real numbers: mid*mid < x is true below the root and false above, so halving a bracket [0, max(1, x)] a fixed number of times pins the root to any precision.
hints: Squaring is monotone on non-negative numbers. If mid*mid < x, which side of mid is the root on?
Bracket the root: it lies in [0, max(1, x)] (for x < 1 the root is larger than x). Halve the bracket, keeping the half whose ends straddle the root.

Run a fixed number of iterations (60-100) rather than 'while hi - lo > eps': doubles have about 52 bits of precision, so a fixed count always terminates. Return the midpoint. Newton's method is the faster alternative.
pitfalls: An absolute epsilon loop can spin forever on huge x where adjacent doubles are further apart than eps.
